node.summary: A workspace participating in the mesh — a repo checkout or an isolated git worktree.
details: Base node vs worktree clone node — a clone isolates parallel work without conflicts.
Shows health (online/offline) alongside git state (branch · ahead/behind · dirty).
Multiple nodes can share the same daemon.

p2p.summary: How the selected coordinator reaches each remote node over WebRTC.
details: direct — a direct host/STUN path; lowest latency.
relay — TURN-relayed; works through restrictive networks but is slower.
disconnected / failed — no live P2P link from the coordinator right now.
P2P connectivity is shown as transport and RTT chips on each node card (and in the node detail panel), not as a graph edge.

session.summary: An agent CLI session running on a node.
details: status = idle / generating / waiting_approval.
Distinguishes coordinator sessions (which dispatch and collect work) from delegated worker sessions (which do the work).

task.summary: A single unit of work handled by the queue-based pull model.
details: States: pending → assigned → completed / failed / cancelled.
Idle nodes claim from the queue automatically; direct dispatch targets a specific session.

mission.summary: A multi-task batch aimed at one goal, and the durable record of that effort.
details: States: active / paused / completed / abandoned.
Progress is derived from the states of its member tasks.

refinery.summary: The process of safely converging and merging a worktree branch into the base.
details: Config-driven (.adhdev/refine.*) — guarded by a patch-equivalence preflight and a no-op guard.
ff-only by principle; no force-push.
If a submodule commit is unreachable from origin it must be published → classified as blocked_review.

completion.summary: Completion of delegated work is persisted to the queue (pending-events).
details: The coordinator learns of completion via periodic polling or events.
Because it is persisted to the queue, completion signals are never lost.

magi.summary: Cross-verification: several independent AI agents answer the same question in parallel.
details: Confidence comes from independence — different AIs on different machines fail in different ways.
When the agents disagree, the disagreement itself flags what to double-check.
Run via mesh_magi_review; the synthesis weighs agreement against source coupling.

magiPanel.summary: A saved, reusable team of (machine × AI) members you invoke by name across investigations.
details: Each member is one provider (AI) optionally pinned to a node (machine), with a replica count.
independent — spans ≥2 providers AND ≥2 machines, so agreement adds real confidence.
coupled — collapses to one AI or one machine; repeated members repeat the same mistakes.
Managed machine-locally from the Panels tab; defined in ~/.adhdev/meshes.json.

convergence.summary: After worktree work, each branch is classified into exactly one final state.
details: merged_to_main — merged into the base.
pushed_feature_branch_needs_merge — pushed, awaiting merge.
blocked_review — held back by review/reachability issues.
cleanup_candidate — ready to clean up.
not_mergeable — cannot be merged.

about.title: About
about.subtitle: Cloud overview, supported surfaces, and plan-level capabilities
about.heroTitle: Control your local CLI agents from anywhere — web or mobile.
about.heroDesc: ADHDev Cloud surfaces the agents running on your machines in your browser: send prompts, approve actions, orchestrate work across machines, and get notified on your phone — code flows P2P directly to your daemon, never through the server.
about.whyDesc: Core capabilities available when your machines are connected through the cloud control plane.
about.howDesc: The cloud onboarding path from install to remote control.
about.repoMeshDesc: Orchestrate agents across machines — cloud only.
about.meshCard1Desc: Enqueue tasks against a mission and let idle nodes claim work from a local-first, pull-based queue. Fan out across machines and providers — Claude Code on one, Codex on another — then converge the results from a single coordinator session.
about.meshCard2Title: Same repo, many machines at once
about.meshCard2Desc: Each node is a checkout or an isolated git worktree, so parallel agents never collide. The refinery converges every branch — validate, merge, push, clean up — with safe submodule handling. Runs over a direct daemon-to-daemon P2P channel; the server only signals and authorizes same-account peers.
about.worksWithDesc: Supported CLI agents, IDEs, and AI extensions.
about.pricingDesc: Current cloud plans and machine capacity by tier.
about.readyDesc: Jump into your dashboard, inspect your connected machines, or continue in the docs if you are still setting up.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy describes how RacoLab ("we", "us", "our") collects, uses, and protects your information when you use the ADHDev service ("Service") at
privacy.s1p1: When you create an account, we collect information provided by your authentication provider (GitHub or Google), including your name, email address, and profile picture.
privacy.s1p2: When you connect your development environment to the Service, the local daemon may transmit:
privacy.s1l2: Active AI agent information (name, status, current model)
privacy.s1l3: Chat messages between you and AI agents
privacy.s1l4: IDE screenshots (transmitted via P2P, not stored on our servers)
privacy.s1l5: Workspace paths and open file names
privacy.s1p3: We automatically collect usage information including API calls, feature usage patterns, and connection logs for service improvement and debugging purposes.
privacy.s1p4: Payment processing is handled entirely by our Merchant of Record, Paddle (Paddle.com Market Limited). We do not directly collect or store credit card numbers, bank account details, or other financial information. Please refer to
privacy.s2l2: Authenticate your identity and manage your account
privacy.s2l3: Route commands and data between your dashboard and connected machines
privacy.s2l4: Send notifications (browser and push) about agent status changes
privacy.s2l5: Process billing and subscription management (via Paddle)
privacy.s2l6: Detect and prevent abuse or unauthorized access
privacy.s2l7: Improve the Service and develop new features
privacy.s3p1: Our Service runs on Cloudflare's global network using Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, and D1 Database. Data is stored in Cloudflare's infrastructure and is subject to
privacy.s3p2: IDE screenshots and real-time terminal data are transmitted directly between your browser and your machine via WebRTC peer-to-peer connections. This data does not pass through or get stored on our servers.
privacy.s3p3: We implement the following security measures:
privacy.s3l1: JWT-based authentication with short-lived access tokens and refresh token rotation
privacy.s3l4: Rate limiting on all API endpoints
privacy.s4p1: We do not sell your personal data to third parties. We may share data with:
privacy.s4l1: Payment processing as Merchant of Record
privacy.s4p2: We may disclose data if required by law, legal process, or to protect our rights and the safety of our users.
privacy.s5p1: We retain your account data for the duration of your active account. Chat messages and agent activity data are retained for up to 90 days for service functionality.
privacy.s5p2: Upon account deletion, we will remove your personal data within 30 days. Some anonymized usage data may be retained for analytical purposes.
privacy.s6l1: Request a copy of your personal data
privacy.s6l2: Update or correct your personal information

hero.badge: The multi-vendor, multi-machine agent control plane
hero.title: Run every local coding agent from the web — in parallel.
hero.subtitle: Drive any CLI agent — Claude Code, Codex, Gemini — from your browser, then scale: orchestrate multiple agents across isolated git worktrees on your own machines and let the Refinery land finished work safely on main, unattended. You talk to one coordinator; it runs the parallel agents asynchronously, so there are no sessions to babysit. P2P — code stays on your machine.
hero.demoDesktop: ADHDev command center driving live agent sessions across multiple machines
hero.demoPush: ADHDev mobile push notification and one-tap approval
hero.scenarioPill: Typical session: assign a mission → agents fan out across Mac + Windows worktrees → the Refinery lands both on main, unattended.

mesh.sectionSubtitle: Spawning parallel agents is the easy part — every tool does it now. The hard part is what happens after: ten branches that still have to be verified and merged. The Refinery does that for you, unattended, so finished work arrives on main instead of in your review queue.
mesh.refineryTitle: Finished work lands on main — unattended
mesh.refineryDesc: Anyone can spawn ten parallel agents. The Refinery validates each worktree against your repo's own gates (typecheck, tests, lint), verifies patch equivalence, publishes submodule commits, fast-forwards main, and cleans up — automatically. No force-push, ever. Anything ambiguous is kicked back for review instead of merged.
mesh.asyncTitle: You talk to one place. It runs the rest.
mesh.asyncDesc: You give work to one coordinator; it drives many workers across many machines on an event loop — reacting only when a completion, approval, or status event arrives. No polling, no window-per-agent to babysit. Unlike a desktop app where you watch each agent session, here the coordinator waits on events, so you don't have to sit synchronously in front of anything.
mesh.crossPlatformTitle: Mac, Windows, Linux — all at once
mesh.crossPlatformDesc: Route tasks to specific OS nodes with a single tag (os=darwin, os=win32, os=linux). One prompt dispatches cross-platform builds, tests, or verifications in parallel across heterogeneous machines you already own. No SSH plumbing, no VMs — just the daemons you already have connected.
mesh.monoDesc: Real production repos nest submodules — and that's exactly where naive auto-merge breaks. The Refinery is submodule-aware: it gates on submodule-commit reachability, judges patch equivalence, and bumps the pointer atomically. This project is itself a root + two-submodule monorepo, converged this way every day.
mesh.crossDesc: Fan the same read-only investigation out to several machine × provider replicas and synthesize where they agree and diverge (MAGI). More trustworthy than one agent's take.
mesh.availableOn: Available on Pro and above. Drive it from the Repo Mesh page once connected.
mesh.graphAlt: Mesh observability after a real converged workstream: mission history, append-only ledger activity, the task queue, and Refinery jobs — feat/get-todo-by-id fast-forwarded into main

compare.sectionTitle: Parallel agents are everywhere now. Where does the work actually land?
compare.sectionSubtitle: A fair question. Local CLIs spawn subagents; desktop orchestrators fan work across worktrees with a slick native UI. Both stop at the branch. Here's the honest line — including where each of them beats us — with no hand-waving.
compare.rowLandsMainLocalCli: You run the gates and merge by hand
compare.rowLandsMainDesktop: Parallelizes the work, then hands you the branches to review
compare.rowLandsMainAdhdev: The Refinery runs your repo's gates, checks patch equivalence, and fast-forwards main — unattended, no force-push
compare.rowSubmodulesLocalCli: No merge automation to be aware of them
compare.rowSubmodulesDesktop: Worktree parallelism, but the merge is yours to get right
compare.rowSubmodulesAdhdev: Submodule-aware convergence: reachability gate, patch-equivalence check, atomic pointer bump — dogfooded on this monorepo daily
compare.rowAsyncLocalCli: One session at a time, synchronously
compare.rowAsyncDesktop: You supervise each agent window yourself
compare.rowAsyncAdhdev: One coordinator drives every worker on an event loop — it waits on completion/approval events, you don't poll or babysit
compare.rowMultiMachineDesktop: Bound to the one machine it runs on
compare.rowMultiMachineAdhdev: Remote daemons over P2P — Mac, Windows, and Linux nodes in one mesh, no SSH plumbing
compare.rowParallelBranchLocalCli: Subagents share one working tree — concurrent writes collide
compare.rowParallelBranchDesktop: One git worktree per task — a core strength
compare.rowParallelBranchAdhdev: One git worktree per node — parallel across machines, not just cores
compare.rowBrowser: Drive it from a browser or phone
compare.rowBrowserLocalCli: You have to be at the terminal
compare.rowBrowserDesktop: Native desktop app — you're at that desk
compare.rowBrowserAdhdev: Web-first: control sessions and approve from any browser or phone
compare.rowNativeAppDesktop: Polished native window — genuinely nicer to sit in front of
compare.rowNativeAppAdhdev: We're web-first — a browser tab, not a native app
compare.rowRestartsLocalCli: State lives in a session — close it and it's gone
compare.rowRestartsDesktop: State tied to the app process
compare.rowRestartsAdhdev: Missions persist to disk and resume after a coordinator or daemon restart — append-only, tamper-evident audit trail
compare.rowCrossCheckLocalCli: One agent's take, no second opinion
compare.rowCrossCheckAdhdev: MAGI fans the same read-only question to independent machine × provider agents and surfaces where they diverge
compare.footnote: For a single machine, a single branch, a one-shot task — a local CLI with subagents is lighter and works great, and a native desktop orchestrator is a nicer place to sit. Repo Mesh earns its keep when work fans out across machines and branches, needs to survive restarts, and should land on main automatically — controlled from wherever you are.

what.sectionSubtitle: Vendor-neutral by design. Run Claude Code on the Mac, Codex on the Windows GPU box, Gemini for review passes — in the same mesh, under the same policies. Switch vendors without switching platforms.
what.cliTitle: Drive any terminal agent from the web
what.cliDesc: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor CLI, Antigravity CLI, Hermes, Kimi, and OpenCode — attached on your machine through a PTY adapter with proper resume and reconnect, driven from your browser. Send prompts and provide visual context instantly (paste, drag & drop, or upload multiple images at once, up to 5 images / 10MB each). Aider, Gemini CLI, Goose, and other ACP agents connect over stdio.
what.uiDesc: Cloud-hosted at adhf.dev — drive every agent from a laptop or phone, whether you're at your desk or away from it.
what.ideDesc: Cursor, VS Code, VSCodium, Windsurf, Antigravity, Kiro, PearAI, Trae. Read live chat, send prompts, switch sessions, capture screenshots.
what.p2pDesc: Chat, commands, and screenshots flow directly between your browser and your daemon over WebRTC. The cloud sees auth and signaling metadata, nothing else — your code never routes through the server.

oss.sectionSubtitle: The daemon and dashboard are AGPL-3.0 and available on GitHub. Run them yourself on any machine or server — no account required.

install.sectionTitle: Three steps to a working dashboard
install.sectionSubtitle: No configuration files. No API keys to wire up. ADHDev does not manage agent auth — each tool keeps its own login.
install.platformNote: macOS and Windows are the validated install paths. Linux runs the same Unix script and is community-tested.

step1.title: Install the daemon
step1.desc: One curl command installs the daemon plus the adhdev CLI — the launcher you run to pair machines and start the daemon (not to be confused with the CLI agents it drives, like Claude Code or Codex). Same binary powers cloud and standalone.

step2.title: Link a machine
step2.desc: Sign in once with GitHub or Google and the daemon pairs itself — no token to copy.

step3.title: Drive your agents
step3.desc: Launch Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor CLI, Antigravity CLI, Hermes, Kimi, and other agents from the dashboard. Read chat, send prompts, provide visual context (paste, drag & drop, or upload multiple images at once), approve actions, and switch sessions.

cta.headline: Stop juggling tabs. Drive every agent from one dashboard.
cta.subtitle: One curl command, one daemon, every agent you already use. Drive them all from the web — Cloud is live.

imagePaste.sectionTitle: Paste a screenshot. A terminal agent on another machine sees it instantly.
imagePaste.sectionSubtitle: Grab a screenshot on your laptop or phone, paste it into the chat, and a CLI agent running in a terminal on a different machine gets it as visual context — no file juggling, no SSH. Paste, drag & drop, or upload up to 5 images (10MB each) at once.

imagePaste.point3: Lands in a PTY terminal agent on any of your machines

mobile.sectionTitle: Leave your desk. Your agents keep going.
mobile.sectionSubtitle: A push notification hits your phone when an agent needs approval or finishes. Tap it, approve or reject, then follow up in chat — all from the mobile dashboard, wherever you are.
mobile.point1: Push notification on approval or completion
mobile.point2: One tap to approve or reject
mobile.point3: Follow up with a chat instruction, then put your phone away
mobile.notificationLabel: Mobile push notification for an agent approval
mobile.resumeLabel: Approving and following up from the mobile dashboard
mobile.point4: No port forwarding, no VPN, no DMZ — P2P with TURN relay connects from cafés, hotspots, anywhere with internet

brain.sectionTitle: Cheap models for easy work. Expensive ones only when it's hard.
brain.sectionSubtitle: Tag a task easy, medium, or difficult and the mesh applies a matching preset — provider, model, and thinking budget. Routine work runs on a cheap fast model; only the hard tasks reach for the expensive one. You spend tokens where they matter.
brain.point2: Each preset picks provider, model, and thinking level
brain.point3: Save tokens without hand-tuning every task

magi.sectionSubtitle: Fan the same read-only question out to a panel of independent agents across different machines and models, then synthesize where they agree and where they diverge — so one model's confident hallucination doesn't slip through as the answer.
magi.point1: Same question, independent machine × model replicas
magi.point2: Surfaces agreement, disagreement, and unique evidence
magi.point3: Catches the one agent that's confidently wrong
magi.origin: Multi-model cross-checking was built into Repo Mesh before it became a trend.
magi.diagramAlt: MAGI fan-out diagram: one read-only question dispatched to independent machine × model replicas, synthesized into agreed, contested, and singleton claims
magi.synthesisAlt: Real MAGI synthesis in the coordinator chat: consensus root cause with file:line evidence, one failed replica reported honestly, and the main conclusion flagged as source-coupled
magi.mediaCaption: Real output from a MAGI run — the failed replica and the source-coupled flag are the honesty, not a bug.

scenario.sectionTitle: One prompt. Mac builds, Windows tests, main lands.
scenario.sectionSubtitle: A real session: you assign a mission, agents fan out across Mac and Windows worktrees in parallel, each validates in isolation, and the Refinery lands both on main — unattended.
scenario.step1Desc: Tell the coordinator what to build. One sentence.
scenario.step2Desc: Tasks dispatch to Mac and Windows nodes simultaneously — each in an isolated git worktree, no shared state.
scenario.step3Desc: Typecheck, tests, lint — your repo's own gates, running in parallel on heterogeneous machines.
scenario.step4Desc: Patch-equivalence check, submodule reachability gate, fast-forward only. Nothing force-pushed.
scenario.step5Desc: Finished work arrives on main. You were never at the terminal.
scenario.caveat: Mac and Windows are the verified daily-driver nodes. Linux is also supported.
